Think on these things, Lipsius, and relieve your own burdens by this communion of miseries. And just as a servant was accustomed to stand behind those celebrating a triumph, frequently shouting in the midst of the joy of the triumph, **You are a man**: so let this monitor always stand by you, **These things are human**. For just as labor shared with many becomes lighter, so too does sorrow.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

->*Conclusion of the entire discourse, and a brief exhortation to review and ruminate upon it.*<-

I have set forth all my resources and discourse, Lipsius, and you have what I deemed necessary to say in favor of Constancy against Sorrow. I wish these things were not only pleasing to you, but also healthy: that they might not just delight, but rather provide aid. They will provide aid, however, if you let them sink not only into your ears, but into your mind: and if you do not allow what has been heard to lie there and wither, like seeds scattered on the surface of the soil.
